question.text: LP Ms. Ananya Singh has committed INR 10 crore to 'Godavari Cat III AIF'. The Manager issues a drawdown notice of 30% with a 10-business-day payment window. Ms. Singh fails to remit on the due date. Under typical AIF agreements, what is the MOST likely immediate consequence for Ms. Singh?

answer.text: Default interest accrues on the unpaid amount, and continued default may lead to reduction of commitment, forfeiture of units, or expulsion as per fund documents
Her full commitment is automatically forfeited and returned to the sponsor
The Manager is personally liable to the fund for her shortfall
The fund must be wound up automatically

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 7 section on default-in-drawdown: the typical mechanism is default interest first, then other LPs may take up the call, with extreme consequences (commitment reduction, forfeiture/expulsion) per the agreement. Not automatic forfeiture. **The Trap:** Option A is too extreme — default is graduated. Option C shifts liability wrongly. Option D fabricates a wind-up consequence. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B test default consequences in general terms; XIX-C tests the graduated mechanism as a Manager. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In the Contribution Agreement, graduate the penalty — e.g., 15% p.a. default interest, followed by 25-50% forfeiture of units after 30 days. This gives you enforcement teeth without having to sue a retail-style LP.
